bundled.built_from: lmms_cpus.c compiled with GCC 11.4 on Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35): gcc -O2 -fPIC -shared -Wl,--build-id=none -o lmms_cpus.so lmms_cpus.c -ldl. The preload limits the processor count visible to LMMS.

modifications: The installer omits the optional VeSTige, Carla base, Carla Rack, Carla Patchbay and external LADSPA host modules; internal instruments and effects retain their upstream bytes. launch.py seeds the normal user configuration and preloads the bundled CPU-count helper; lmms_cpus.c is included. isolation.py confines reference filesystem access and external program execution without changing the upstream binary.
configuration: launch.py seeds HOME/.lmmsrc.xml once (first-run dialogs skipped, SDL audio on the PulseAudio sink, dummy MIDI, autosave off, LMMS working directory = PBP_FILES_DIR) and execs runtime/usr/bin/lmms.real with LD_LIBRARY_PATH set only for it and with lmms_cpus.so preloaded, which reports at most LMMS_CPUS processors (the CPU quota, the allowed processors and 4, whichever is smallest) so LMMS starts no more mixer threads than its quota allows; with arguments it runs the LMMS command line (render, rendertracks, dump, upgrade) The document exchange rejects external plugin-host declarations, external entities and oversized compressed project text. Landlock is required; filesystem rights are limited to those supported by the kernel ABI; the product can write only its instance/exchange directories and execute only its own main executable and dynamic loader. External library-host modules are absent from the installed product. The native executable starts in the document workspace so file choosers do not enumerate the installation root.

notes.component_notices: Bundled distribution copyright notices are reproduced in LICENSES and remain in runtime/usr/share/doc; factory data keeps its original notices.
